_README:
Canonical face per person, so anyone appearing in several seasons looks the same in all of them. Apply as the LAST step of any build, after appearances are sourced or generated.
  "faces"       — players, keyed "normalized name|position"
  "staff_faces" — coaches, scouts and physios, keyed on normalized name alone (a coach can change role between years, so position is not part of the key)
Priority: Ryan's in-game export first (those are his hand edits), then 2004, 2007, 2013, 2010, 2017.
To add hand edits: diff a fresh in-game export against the source file and write the changed records in at top priority.
Before this existed, Belichick had five different faces across five files and Tom Brady had five.
  "faces_1986" — 1986-season players, keyed "normalized name|position|teamID". TEAM IS PART OF THE KEY: name+position is not unique even within one season (two different James Joneses, both RB, in 1986). SEPARATE from "faces" ON PURPOSE. A reader that does not know about this block ignores it, which is the correct behaviour for a 2004-2026 build: across a 35-year gap, name+position matching is wrong far more often than right (measured 3 of 16 correct; Clay Matthews, Kellen Winslow and Mickey Shuler are fathers whose sons share name AND position). Names here KEEP generational suffixes — the main registry's norm() strips them, which collapses father and son. Scope note: the registry's rule is players appearing in more than one file; these appear in one. Written deliberately anyway, because these faces are the only ones that will exist for these men unless a future 1985/1990 build reproduces them from scratch, and several are better sourced than a later build could manage (skin from a decoded Xbox 360 roster field, facial hair from photographs). The justification rests on such a build eventually existing; if none is made, this block is harmless dead weight rather than an error.
  "staff_faces_1986" — 1986-season staff, keyed on normalized name alone, matching the "staff_faces" convention (a coach changes role between years). SEPARATE from "faces_1986" so a name-only key can never collide with a name|position|teamID one. Free agents carry the literal teamID "Free Agent" in the third key field: measured on the 1986 free agent pool, name+position is already unique (0 collisions among 201 players, 0 among 150 staff), so the team field is there for shape and for separating a free agent from a rostered man of the same name and position, not because it was needed to disambiguate.
_normalization: lowercase, strip punctuation and Jr/Sr/II/III/IV/V, collapse initials
_scope: Rebuilt 2026-08-31. faces_1986 and staff_faces_1986 are ERA-SCOPED: 1986 faces, keyed name|position|teamID. Do NOT read them for a modern build - across a 35-year gap only 3 of 16 name+position matches were the same man, the rest were fathers and sons. Skin comes from a decoded Xbox 360 Madden field (bit 1347, width 2: 0=light, 1=dark, 2=Pacific Islander/Hispanic) mapped to families per position against the published distribution, with side as a hard constraint. 78 players carry hand-verified faces from photographs - skin, hair colour, hair STYLE and facial hair - which is the only real hairstyle data anywhere in the project.
_verified:
Keys listed here carry faces the project owner set by hand, in game, against photographs. They are the highest-confidence appearance data in the project and the ONLY real hairstyle and facial-hair data anywhere in it - every other player's hair style and beard are assigned, not sourced. DO NOT OVERWRITE these in any rebuild. A derived-appearance pass must skip any key present here. Format matches the block it refers to: player keys are name|position|teamID, staff keys are name.

LOCKED (2026-08-31 ruling): anything Ryan sets by hand in game — player or coach — is verified and must never be overwritten by any automated pass, however good the source scores. A pass that disagrees with a verified key skips it and logs the disagreement; it does not win. This block previously held only 1986 faces; the 2004 in-game edits were mistakenly filed as _labelled_keys and the EA consensus pass then overwrote Tony Gonzalez's hand-set Head3b.
